item.title: SALSATECA FIESTA! — Sat Aug 29, 7:00 PM — WCKUK Lewisham
item.description: Your Salsa, Bachata and Cuban Party in Lewisham On the last Saturday of Every Month Learn Salsa, learn Bachata! Have fun and meet new friends!​ Our regular Saturdays become a party on the last Saturday of every month. Experience an unforgettable Salsa & Bachata Party at the Zhulin Hidden Village in Lewisham. We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Many attendees come solo, and we rotate partners throughout the lesson, giving you the chance to dance with different people. If you’d prefer to stay with your own partner for the entire class, just let the teacher know, and we’ll be happy to accommodate you. Since most Latin parties feature both Salsa and Bachata, learning both is not only fun but also a must! So, we strongly recommend and encourage our students to learn both. SCHEDULE: 7pm to 8pm: SALSA (Cross Body Style) Beginners

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Smaller and More Robotic — Tue Sep 1, 12:00 AM — Oakwood Village Library and Arts Centre
item.description: Throughout the month of September, the works of artist Jay Rangam are on display at Oakwood Village Library Arts Centre. Jay Rangam is an artist that lives and works in Toronto, Canada. He received his MFA from the Maryland Institute College of Art in 2021 and his BFA from OCAD University in 2019. He has exhibited in group shows in Toronto, Montreal, Baltimore and New York. My recent paintings from 2024 - 2025 begin with digitally combining drawings that I’ve used in previous bodies of work to create new images. Using the digital cartoon as a starting point for painting, the application of different materials and colours is intended to abstract the representational subject matter of the drawings, creating paintings that appear somewhat abstract while retaining traces of a relationship to the natural world. item.title: Civic Meetup #559: Creeped Out: Privacy and Discrimination Risks of Health-related Machine Listening — Tue Sep 8, 7:00 PM — Online: https://link.civictech.ca/zoom / Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario
item.description:
New technologies and organizations’ practices are regularly placing pressures and challenges on our privacy and transparency rights. This month, Civic Tech Toronto and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario are highlighting the work to defend, enforce, explain and update these rights.
‎‎
Topic: Creeped Out: Privacy and Discrimination Risks of Health-related Machine Listening
Typical arguments about creepy technology focus on the visceral ‘ick’ factor of innovation. In contrast, this talk shares a methodology to track patterns of function creep and empirically assess changing privacy and discrimination risks. The research focuses on the product development and deployment of health-related machine listening: apps and devices that combine audio signal processing and machine learning techniques to produce sensitive inferences about people’s health from data points such as vocal biomarkers, coughs, infant cries, and other sounds. item.title: Elections 101: Preparing for the 2026 Toronto Municipal Election — Tue Sep 15, 5:30 PM — Parkdale
item.description:
The 2026 Toronto Municipal Election takes place on Monday, October 26. Join Toronto Elections for an informative session covering everything you need to know to cast your ballot with confidence. Learn about municipal elections, voting dates and times, voting options, and accessibility supports available to voters. We will also demonstrate MyVote , Toronto Elections' online tool that provides personalized voting information. Whether you're a first-time or future voter, new to Toronto, or simply looking to learn more about the municipal election process, this session will help you feel more informed and ready to participate in your local democracy. Check out the KnowYourVote.TO website and the Celebrate Democracy page to learn more about Toronto’s upcoming municipal election, access important voter resources, and discover activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.

item.title: Frontenac Fall Colours Hike — Sat Sep 26, 7:00 AM
item.description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club **Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fall-colours-frontenac)**
**A true member favourite returns! While the crowds flock to Algonquin to view fall colours, Frontenac is where it's really at.**
By late September, the first maples along this loop are already turning red and gold against bare granite, weeks ahead of peak colour further south. That granite is part of the Frontenac Arch, a two-billion-year-old ridge connecting the Canadian Shield to the Adirondacks, and it's what gives this loop its particular look in fall.
The Cedar Lake South Loop runs about 9km through a mix of open granite, rooted forest trails, and genuine wetland: expect boggy sections, small ponds, and stretches where the water clearly has the upper hand on the trail.

item.title: History of Philosophy Research Group Talk (Bridger Ehli, IU-Bloomington) — Thu Oct 15, 3:00 PM — Jackman Humanities Building
item.description:
The History of Modern Philosophy Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Bridger Ehli, an assistant professor in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Indiana – Bloomington. His research concerns themes in epistemology, metaphysics, and the philosophy of mind in early modern European philosophy. He is especially interested in early modern discussions of skepticism, especially as they relate to questions about mental representation, concepts, and the psychology of belief. Most of his work has focused on Hume’s contributions to these issues. In a forthcoming book, he argues that much of Hume’s skepticism arises from his thinking about the limits of intelligibility rather than those of justified belief. Details to follow.
